questions.question: What is Mr. Popper's job?
questions.explanation: Mr. Popper works as a house painter, but only during the warmer months when paint can dry properly.

questions.question: Where does the first penguin come from?
questions.explanation: Admiral Drake sends Captain Cook to Mr. Popper as a gift from his expedition in Antarctica.

questions.question: What is the name of the first penguin?
questions.explanation: Mr. Popper names the penguin Captain Cook, after the famous explorer.

questions.question: What does Captain Cook like to eat?
questions.explanation: Like all penguins, Captain Cook eats fish. Mr. Popper had to buy fish from the market.

questions.question: Where does Captain Cook like to sleep?
questions.explanation: Captain Cook sleeps in the refrigerator because penguins need cold temperatures.

questions.question: What is the name of the female penguin sent to be Captain Cook's companion?
questions.explanation: Greta is sent from an aquarium to be Captain Cook's companion when he becomes lonely.

questions.question: How many baby penguins do Captain Cook and Greta have?
questions.explanation: Captain Cook and Greta have ten baby penguins, making the total twelve penguins.

questions.question: What do the Poppers do to make money with the penguins?
questions.explanation: The Poppers train the penguins to perform tricks and they travel to theaters putting on shows.

questions.question: What is the name of the town where the Poppers live?
questions.explanation: The Popper family lives in the town of Stillwater.

questions.question: Where do the penguins go at the end of the story?
questions.explanation: Admiral Drake takes the penguins to the North Pole to start a new penguin colony there.

questions.question: Why was Captain Cook sad and not eating?
questions.explanation: Captain Cook was lonely because penguins are social animals. He needed another penguin for company.

questions.question: What did Mr. Popper do to keep the penguins cool in the house?
questions.explanation: Mr. Popper had a freezing plant installed in the basement to keep the house cold enough for twelve penguins.

questions.question: What kind of food did the penguins eat while traveling on tour?
questions.explanation: While on the road, the penguins ate canned shrimps because they were easier to transport than fresh fish.

questions.question: What is the name of the penguin theater act?
questions.explanation: The act was called 'Popper's Performing Penguins' and became famous across the country.

questions.question: What song did Mrs. Popper play for the penguin drill?
questions.explanation: Mrs. Popper played the 'Military March' on the piano while the penguins marched in formation.

questions.question: What happens to Mr. Popper at the end of the book?
options: He stays home to paint houses
He goes to the North Pole with the penguins
questions.explanation: Mr. Popper decides to join Admiral Drake's expedition and go to the North Pole with his beloved penguins.

questions.question: What is the name of the street where the Poppers live?
questions.explanation: The Popper family lives at 432 Proudfoot Avenue in the town of Stillwater.

questions.question: What is the title of the book Mr. Popper reads in Chapter II?
questions.explanation: Mr. Popper reads 'Antarctic Adventures' to learn more about the polar regions he loves so much.

questions.question: What did Captain Cook eat in the dining room that made Mrs. Popper angry?
questions.explanation: Captain Cook ate the goldfish from the bowl in the dining room, which upset Mrs. Popper.

questions.question: How many air holes did the service man drill in the refrigerator door?
questions.explanation: The service man drilled five air holes in the refrigerator door so Captain Cook could breathe while sleeping inside.

questions.question: What did the policeman first think Captain Cook was?
questions.explanation: When the policeman first saw Captain Cook, he thought the penguin was a giant parrot because he had never seen a penguin before.

questions.question: What did Mr. Popper use as a leash for Captain Cook?
questions.explanation: Mr. Popper used a clothesline as a leash when taking Captain Cook for walks around town.

questions.question: What was Captain Cook's temperature when he was very sick?
questions.explanation: When Captain Cook was very ill, his temperature rose to 104 degrees, which worried the Poppers greatly.

questions.question: Which two penguins usually get into a fight with each other?
questions.explanation: Nelson and Columbus were always fighting with each other, which caused problems during their performances.

questions.question: How much money per week did the penguins earn on their contract?
questions.explanation: The penguins earned $5,000 per week on their theater contract, which was a huge amount of money.

questions.question: Why was Mr. Popper arrested in New York?
options: For going to the wrong theater
questions.explanation: Mr. Popper was arrested because he accidentally went to the wrong theater (the Regal) instead of the Royal.

questions.question: Who offered Mr. Popper a contract to put the penguins in movies?
questions.explanation: Mr. Klein, a Hollywood movie producer, offered the Poppers a contract to put their penguins in films.
